value: sensible heat storage: a liquid or solid medium (water, sand, rocks, concrete, molten salt) heated or cooled and kept in an insulated tank or underground; water tanks up to 80-90 degC charging, oil or molten salt above 100 degC (salt to 550 degC), ceramics and concrete for very high temperatures; cheapest TES but low energy density (about 25 kWh/m3) and a discharge temperature that falls as the store empties
note: Table 1 is generic across buildings, district heating and industry; the brief does not split industrial values out. Table 1's row is labelled 'Sensible (hot water)'.

value: latent heat storage in phase change materials (PCM): heat stored in a solid/liquid (or solid/solid) phase change at a fixed temperature, giving a constant discharge temperature and about 100 kWh/m3 (e.g. ice) against about 25 kWh/m3 for sensible storage; materials from ice (0 degC) and paraffins (-5 to 120 degC) to salt hydrates and sugar alcohols (erythritol 118 degC); industrial R&D targets high-temperature PCM above 150 degC
